body:
A real finding, well-sampled this time, and it partly vindicates the perf bead whose headline numbers I refuted.

Profiled 60 consecutive rdm_sampling_covariance() calls on the Haxby VT exemplar configuration - 577 features, 577 centres, support 44.8, q=8, fixed metric - JIT warmed by 5 prior calls. 3192 samples at 2 ms, so the percentages are trustworthy, unlike my earlier 36-sample profile.

  TOTAL TIME
    .require_relation_fit_capability      53.4 percent
    relation_fit_capabilities             53.0 percent
    .validate_relation                    17.8 percent
    grepl                                 14.2 percent
    .additive_frame_signature              9.5 percent

  SELF TIME, top: grepl 14.2, serialize 5.9, deparse 4.4, make.names 3.5, digest 2.6
  steady-state per call: 0.106 s

MORE THAN HALF OF EVERY CALL IS RE-DERIVING CAPABILITY INFORMATION ABOUT THE FIT. That result is a property of the fit and cannot change across nodes of a sweep. Computing it once and carrying it on the fit or the plan removes about half the per-call cost without changing any returned number.

And serialize, deparse, make.names and digest in the top self-time entries, plus .additive_frame_signature at 9.5 percent, say signatures are recomputed per call. For a fixed plan and fixed fit those cannot differ between node 1 and node 577.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC. That bead's figures did not reproduce - 0.65 s/node by the script's own clock against a claimed 9 - but its stated suspicion was 'per-call recomputation of plan/fit-invariant work (residual factorization, contrasts, validation)'. Validation was the right guess. It is now quantified. I filed it separately, bd-01KZZWP1PA6N3NZQGZ1S9JTH1Q, so it survives whatever disposition the parent gets: the parent rests on a number I could not reproduce, this one rests on a measurement I could.

Scale, stated conservatively: at 0.106 s/node a 577-centre sweep is about 61 seconds. Halving that is not the difference between usable and unusable - the arm is already usable, contrary to the README - but it is a straightforward halving of the package's most expensive documented operation, and the work removed is provably invariant.

Caveat: profiler attribution misleads when functions inline or when something cheap is called very often. Before restructuring, cache the capability result behind a flag and re-measure. That is a much smaller change than the precompute-once object the parent bead proposes, and it tests the hypothesis directly.

Method note, since I have been burned repeatedly today: my first profile of this function sampled 36 points and I read percentages off it. That was not enough to say anything. This one has 3192. The earlier one happened to point at the same functions, but that was luck, and I should not have quoted it.
